operations.specification:
This operation allows a new 'user' actor to register an account and receive their initial authentication tokens. Only users not already registered can access this endpoint. The account creation process uses fields defined in the user table, such as email, password, and any user identity fields present in the schema. The primary goal is to enable a new user to onboard and immediately start managing their personal todo list. The registration process validates the uniqueness of the email and enforces all password requirements as stated in the actor and business rules. If registration succeeds, a JWT access and refresh token pair is returned following the system's token management policies. No additional data is created beyond the user record and initial session.

The endpoint is public and requires no prior authentication. If the email already exists, a detailed error is returned describing the constraint failure. The design references actual field names and constraints within the user table schema.

Upon success, the response includes a DTO containing tokens, user info, and session meta as defined for ITodoListUser.IAuthorized. Token issuance and user identity include only fields defined in the user schema. Session and login events may be logged if supported.

All validations (such as password policy or input sanitation) follow the business requirements and existing user schema definitions. The endpoint is compatible with automation and external client onboarding if required.

This operation is a critical entry point for authentication flow and is related to the login and refresh endpoints. Together, they comprise the complete user authentication suite for this actor.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows registration and onboarding of a new registered user by inserting a record into the user database table, validating unique fields such as email according to schema constraints, and issuing authentication tokens as described in the user requirements. The registration logic enforces the password policy, field uniqueness, and all validation rules defined in the Prisma schema for the user table. The endpoint is unauthenticated and available for public registration.

Upon success, it returns a token-based authentication DTO (ITodoListUser.IAuthorized) containing the access and refresh tokens, user ID, and any meta-information as described in the schema comments. Any fields returned are strictly those defined in the user schema. Error responses are structured based on unique constraint or validation failures. The authentication workflow is completed on registration: no email verification or multi-factor is enforced unless explicitly described in the schema.

This endpoint is part of the user authentication suite (join, login, refresh) and is distinct from profile or user management APIs. Fields and data provided to this operation are strictly those defined in the user schema. Security policies for registration rate limiting, input sanitation, and auditing are enforced where described in requirements. Related operations include login and refresh, which are needed after registration for continued session management.

The endpoint aligns with modern public API practices for onboarding and can be integrated into automated registration flows. It does not allow duplicate registrations or bypass field validation rules. All relevant business and validation rules from requirements are enforced.

It is recommended to review the field requirements in the user schema before implementing client integration or custom UI flows.
operations.summary: Register a new user account and receive authentication tokens (todo_list_users table).

requestBody.description: Registration data for a new user as defined in the todo_list_users Prisma schema. Fields must include only those defined for the user entity.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user info per ITodoListUser.IAuthorized DTO returned on successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
This endpoint authenticates an existing user actor using credentials defined in the user table, such as email and password (using the exact schema field names). On successful authentication, it issues new JWT tokens following system token management policies. This is used for normal user login to obtain access tokens for further API calls.

Credential validation uses the stored password hash and checks for account existence using indexed user fields. The implementation references the user Prisma schema so only available fields participate in authentication. Error handling includes clear messages for invalid credentials or unrecognized accounts but does not disclose information that could be abused for enumeration. The endpoint is designed for public login and cannot be used by users not previously registered.

On success, returns a DTO containing tokens and authorized session info matching ITodoListUser.IAuthorized, as well as any session management data if supported by the underlying schema. Related endpoints are join (for registration) and refresh (for token renewal).

Security policies—for example, rate limiting, failed login lockouts, or IP restriction—are described in the requirements and must be enforced as described, but only using available user table fields. The endpoint must not support any operations beyond login and token grant, and should avoid unnecessary exposure of user data.

This endpoint is fundamental for all further user-level actions and integrates with the refresh token and session management operations for the user actor.
operations.description:
This operation allows a registered user to authenticate by sending their credentials (typically email and password, referencing actual user table fields) to determine access. The endpoint checks the credentials against the stored values in the todo_list_users Prisma schema. On a successful match, a new JWT access/refresh token pair is issued and structured as an ITodoListUser.IAuthorized DTO.

All credential validation and security policies (password hashes, failed login attempts, account status checks) use fields defined in the user schema. The endpoint is part of the user authentication suite and enables further authenticated API use. Security and validation policies (rate limiting, input sanitation) are enforced per requirements and available schema constraints.

It returns only the tokens and necessary user/session information as defined by requirements and schema, with no exposure of additional PII. The login route is unauthenticated for input but issues tokens only on successful credential match.

Error responses are clearly defined: invalid combinations receive a generic failure message per best security practices. This endpoint, combined with join and refresh, forms the complete authentication system for the user actor.
operations.summary: Authenticate existing user with credentials and receive tokens (todo_list_users table).

requestBody.description: Login credentials for an existing user from todo_list_users Prisma schema (e.g., email, password). Only use fields that exist in the schema.

responseBody.description: Tokens, session info, and user identity per ITodoListUser.IAuthorized returned on successful authentication.

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
This operation allows an authenticated user actor to renew their session using a valid refresh token. It is called as part of the JWT session flow to obtain a new pair of authentication tokens. The endpoint expects a refresh token as provided at login/registration, using the exact field name(s) required by requirements. The token validation and renewal process follows business rules for session management and security described in requirements and limited to the capabilities of the schema.

If the provided refresh token is valid and the session can be extended (per user session table, if present), a new ITodoListUser.IAuthorized DTO with updated tokens is returned. Error handling includes generic failures if the token is invalid, expired, or otherwise unusable. The endpoint does not expose internal state or error codes that could be abused.

This endpoint is essential for seamless client-side token renewal and maintaining authenticated sessions for the user actor. It is closely related to the join and login endpoints and is part of the standard user authentication flow.
operations.description:
Allows an authenticated user to refresh their access and refresh tokens by presenting a valid (unexpired) refresh token. The endpoint checks token validity and session continuity based on fields and structures supported by the todo_list_users and (optionally) todo_list_user_sessions schemas. It returns a new ITodoListUser.IAuthorized DTO containing refreshed tokens, user identity (as in schema), and meta/session info. Any session management is performed per requirements and schema capability.

Input and output strictly follow schema field requirements and only use session or user fields that are present. The endpoint is used after login or registration to keep user sessions alive without re-authenticating with credentials. Security, expiration, and session policies are applied per requirements and schema design.

Related endpoints: login, join (for session initiation); this endpoint forms the last leg of the authentication suite. Error responses are generic to prevent token enumeration or abuse. The endpoint cannot be used for other session or account management operations.
operations.summary: Refresh user JWT tokens with a valid refresh token (todo_list_users table).

requestBody.description: The refresh token, as defined in requirements and schema. Only actual fields are accepted.

responseBody.description: A new set of tokens and session info in ITodoListUser.IAuthorized format.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated, filterable list of user accounts registered within the Todo List application. It reads from the todo_list_users table, which stores core user authentication data such as email addresses and password hashes. This endpoint is designed strictly for administrative or technical inspection purposes, not for user self-service or registration flows. The operation supports advanced search and filtering by email address, in anticipation of future expansion (such as email domain or account registration period). This enables system oversight for tasks like audit, de-duplication, compliance, and debugging.
operations.description:
Fetch a filtered and paginated list of all registered user accounts in the Todo List system.

This operation is intended for administrative use only. It exposes user emails and identity fields solely for security auditing, investigating registration issues, or for compliance with business reporting requirements. This endpoint never exposes password hashes or sensitive authentication materials in the response; such details are strictly internal.

Filtering, pagination, and future extensibility for searching by various criteria are supported by request body parameters. The underlying table enforces uniqueness on the email field, assuring that all users listed are uniquely identified. As per the data minimization requirement, the fields returned include only email and minimally necessary identity details. No profile, role, or irreversibly deleted accounts are involved, per the schema and business policy.

All usage is strictly governed by strong authentication and authorization policies, and only system administrators have access to this data. Common uses include reviewing system registrations, identifying duplicate or fraudulent emails, and compliance reporting.
operations.summary: Retrieve a paginated and filterable list of user accounts from the todo_list_users table.

requestBody.description: Optional search and pagination parameters for user list retrieval.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of summary user account information (only non-sensitive fields).

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the details of a single user account by its unique ID, reading from the todo_list_users table in the Todo List system. It enables administrative use cases such as investigating user account issues, compliance review, technical debugging, or system audit. This endpoint never exposes password hashes or related authentication secrets. The ID must correspond to a currently registered user; no endpoints exist for deleted or pending users. This operation does not support modification, creation, or deletion of account records, in line with the business requirement that only registered and active user data may be viewed administratively. All access is strictly limited to system administrators, enforcing appropriate separation of duties.
operations.description:
Fetch non-sensitive detail for a specific registered user account, identified by unique system ID.

This administrative endpoint is used for investigation, compliance, or technical debugging. The only data accessible are minimal user account identifiers (such as email); password hashes are never provided. The 'userId' parameter matches the primary key in the todo_list_users table.

All user account access is tightly governed by authentication and authorization checks: only system administrators are permitted to view user account records. This operation is never exposed to end-users or used for self-service, authentication, or registration workflows. All requested information must be in compliance with the data minimization and hard deletion business policy.
operations.summary: Retrieve non-sensitive details of a single user from the todo_list_users table by unique ID.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user account (UUID primary key in todo_list_users).

responseBody.description: The detailed user account entity (excluding password hash and secrets).

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing user account in the Todo List application. It operates on the todo_list_users table. The user account is uniquely identified by the UUID id path parameter, which is the primary key for each record in the table. The request body must include all mutable fields allowed for update, such as email and password_hash, ensuring only valid domain fields are supported and following the security requirements outlined in the schema documentation. Updates enforce uniqueness for the email field and recalculate password hashes using secure algorithms.
operations.description:
Update the details for a single Todo List user account as identified by their unique userId.

This API operation allows modification of user-specific properties including email and password. The input requires the full payload of mutable fields in the user table. Security best practices mandate that emails remain unique within the system and password hashes are never stored in plaintext. All write actions are immediately committed to the database, as there is no support for soft deletion or audit trails.

This endpoint is protected: only the authenticated user may update their own account. Updates to the user account do not affect any user-created todos or other records, but maintaining an up-to-date email ensures continued access and notifications. Any attempt to update non-existent fields or protected properties will result in a validation error. All updates trigger a full validation and the updated user record is returned on success.
operations.summary: Update an existing Todo List user account by userId (todo_list_users table).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user account

requestBody.description: Updated data for the user account, such as a new email or password hash. Must comply with all validation rules and uniqueness constraints.

responseBody.description: Updated user account details after successful modification.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a user account from the todo_list_users table by its unique UUID id. Deletion is immediate and irreversible, aligning with the strict privacy and hard delete business rules described in the schema. This operation ensures that all authentication and account data for the specified user are fully removed from the system, with no retention or recovery of deleted data.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a Todo List user account as specified by the userId. This operation enforces the policy that all account deletions are hard deletes: once a user is deleted, all credentials and personal data are removed and cannot be recovered. No soft delete or retention period is implemented in this application.

The endpoint is strictly protected so that only the account owner may delete their own record. Cascading effects are limited; todos previously owned by the deleted user may remain in the system as orphaned records or will be subject to hard deletion by related business rules, depending on foreign key constraints. Data minimization requirements are enforced to prevent retention of any personal information after deletion. Improper requests or missing records result in error responses.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a Todo List user account by userId (todo_list_users table).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user account

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves all session records associated with a given user from the todo_list_user_sessions table. It enables inspection or security auditing of all authentication sessions held by a specific user. Sessions include contextual metadata such as the originating IP address, connection URL, referrer information, session creation timestamp, and (if applicable) the session expiration timestamp. This API is designed for audit, monitoring, and forensic investigation to help ensure integrity of user authentication activity. Individual session details can be further retrieved using the GET session endpoint. Listing sessions is never available to normal users and is strictly for security and backend maintenance purposes. It supports filtering, sorting, and pagination in the request body; results are paginated session summary records. The owning user's unique identifier (id, UUID format) is provided as a required path parameter.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of all session records for a specific user account by privileged system access. This API is intended for audit or investigation of user login activities in the todo list application.

The session records contain metadata for each authentication session, including client IP, referrer, connection URL, and lifecycle timestamps. Only the system or internally authorized components are expected to use this endpoint for reviewing authentication history, tracking potential security issues, and managing session policy.

Sensitive information such as password hashes are never returned, and all business rules for data minimization and audit trail integrity, as specified in the Prisma schema, are tightly enforced. Pagination is supported for efficient navigation through large record sets. The related user account is referenced by UUID in the path, and session records are sorted by creation time by default.
operations.summary: List all sessions for a user (todo_list_user_sessions).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the user whose session records are being listed.

requestBody.description: Search, filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria for session listing.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of summary session records for the target user.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information about a single session record from the todo_list_user_sessions table, identified by its unique session ID (UUID), belonging to a specific user. Intended for audit and traceability, it provides session metadata such as originating IP, connection URL, referrer, and precise creation/expiration timestamps. This endpoint allows in-depth investigation into individual sessions to support troubleshooting and incident response. The operation never exposes user credential details or sensitive private data and is strictly restricted to system or privileged use. Both the user's ID (UUID) and the session's ID (UUID) are required as path parameters. The response delivers the detailed session record for inspection.
operations.description:
Retrieve full detail for a specific authentication session associated with the indicated user. This API is intended for system or backend component use, for security and audit review of user sessions in the todo list service.

Each session record provides contextual metadata about the authentication event, including the originating IP, HTTP referrer, connection URL, and full authentication lifecycle timestamps (creation and, if available, expiration).

Both the user's ID and the session's ID are required in the path. Only privileged system-level logic may access this information; users cannot inspect session records for themselves or others directly via API. Sensitive attributes, such as credential hashes, are never returned; only audit-appropriate information is exposed as defined in the Prisma schema.
operations.summary: Get details of a specific session for a user (todo_list_user_sessions).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the user who owns the session.

parameters.name: userSessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the session to retrieve for the specified user.

responseBody.description: Detailed session record for the indicated user session.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation deletes a user session for a specific user in the Todo List application. It is associated with the todo_list_user_sessions Prisma DB table, which tracks all authentication sessions for users. The operation enforces a hard deletion of the session record, permanently removing it from the database. Only users themselves may delete their own sessions, and this action ensures session logs are irreversibly removed per strict security and privacy requirements. The operation requires both the userId and userSessionId as path parameters—each represented as a UUID. Users typically invoke this endpoint during logout from a device or when terminating sessions after a password reset.
operations.description:
Delete a specific user session for a given user from the system.

This operation is intended to allow users to log out of or forcibly terminate sessions associated with their account, for example when logging out from a device or after changing their password.

The session record is permanently removed from the database. There is no soft deletion or session recovery; this operation complies with strict privacy and security rules for the Todo List application.

The operation strictly enforces that only the owner can delete their own session, ensuring there is no cross-account manipulation. Path parameters userId and userSessionId are both required, and must be valid UUID format. If the session does not exist or does not belong to the user, an error is returned.

Related operations include login (handled by the authentication service) and session retrieval (admin auditing only, not user-facing).
operations.summary: Delete a user session record from the todo_list_user_sessions table.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the user who owns the session.

parameters.name: userSessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the user session to be deleted.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation performs a paginated search and retrieval of todo items for the Todo List application, operating on the todo_list_todos Prisma DB table. It allows authenticated users to query their own todos based on completion status, title substring, and creation/update date ranges. The endpoint enforces strict per-user data access so that users may only list their own tasks. Pagination and search support efficient listing even with a large number of personal todos. Results include summaries for display in clients, incorporating the is_completed state and timestamps. The associated user is inferred from the authentication context, not passed as a path parameter.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of todo items for the authenticated user.

This operation supports searching by title substring, filtering by is_completed state, and specifying ranges on creation and last update timestamps. All results are scoped so that each user may only see their own todos—cross-user access is strictly prohibited.

Pagination parameters control result set size and offset. Sorting by created_at or updated_at fields is supported. Response data is in summary form, suitable for list display (showing core fields like title, status, and timestamps). The operation references the todo_list_todos table and includes all validation and privacy enforcement per requirements.

Related operations include GET for single todo retrieval, POST for creation, PUT for updates, and DELETE for removal. This PATCH operation is specialized for advanced list searching and efficient pagination.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of a user's todos from the todo_list_todos table.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, pagination parameters, and filters for querying todos. All filters apply only to the authenticated user's own todos.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summaries matching the provided search criteria and filters.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the details of a specific todo item by its globally unique identifier (UUID). It is based on the todo_list_todos table from the Prisma database, which stores all personal todo items for the Todo List application. Every todo entry is linked to its owner user via a foreign key to todo_list_users, and only the owner is authorized to access their todos. The operation ensures strict per-user data privacy—if a user attempts to access a todo not owned by them, an authorization error is returned. The response includes all fields for the todo, such as title, optional description, completion status, and timestamps for both creation and last update. This API endpoint is essential for users to view task details and supports client-side workflows for displaying or further editing of a todo item.
operations.summary: Retrieve a specific todo by its unique identifier from the todo_list_todos table.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of a todo item by its unique identifier.

This operation allows an authenticated user to obtain all information about one of their own todos by specifying the todo's unique identifier in the URL path parameter. The response includes the todo's required title, optional description, boolean completion status, and timestamps for creation and last modification as defined in the todo_list_todos table. All field constraints and descriptions are consistent with the schema documentation to ensure reliable access and presentation at the client layer.

Security is strictly enforced—users may only access todo items they personally own. If a user requests a todo that does not exist or does not belong to them, the system will return an appropriate error without revealing information about other users' data. This operation does not require or accept a request body, and is typically used to support detailed views or editing flows on the client side. Related operations include listing the user's todos, creating a new todo, updating properties, and deleting a todo.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo item to retrieve, must be a valid UUID corresponding to an existing todo belonging to the authenticated user.

responseBody.description: The complete details of the requested todo item, including all its stored fields as defined in the todo_list_todos schema.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A todo must be created before it can be retrieved by its unique identifier. This ensures that the requested todoId corresponds to an existing todo entity belonging to the user.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item and assigns it to the authenticated user, leveraging the todo_list_todos table for persistent storage. It requires a non-empty title and optionally accepts a description, both subject to the schema-defined validation rules. The completion status is set to false and timestamps are recorded automatically on creation. Business requirements for ownership, privacy, and immediate visibility in the user's todo list are enforced—no other user may view or manipulate the created todo. Authorization is strictly tied to the initiating user, and field validation (length, required properties) is performed according to detailed requirements and schema comments. Upon success, the operation returns the full newly-created todo entity including all default and assigned fields.
operations.summary: Create a new todo for the authenticated user in the todo_list_todos table.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item and associate it with the authenticated user.

This operation enables a user to add a new todo to their private list by submitting a request containing a title (required) and an optional description. Input values are validated in accordance with the input validation and business rules: the title must be a non-empty string of up to 255 characters, not only whitespace, and the description, if provided, must be up to 1024 characters. Upon successful validation, the todo is created with the authenticated user's ID as owner, its is_completed status set to false, and both creation and update timestamps recorded per the schema definition.

Privacy is fundamental—todos are strictly personal, visible and accessible only to their owner. If input validation fails, the system provides explicit error messages describing the failed field and reason. The response contains the full newly-created todo entity so clients may update their UI immediately. Related operations include viewing, updating, or deleting a todo, and listing all todos belonging to the user.

requestBody.description: Fields for creating a new todo: a required title and optional description. Both fields must comply with length and content validation. The new todo is automatically assigned to the authenticated user and initialized with is_completed as false.

responseBody.description: The fully constructed todo entity as stored, reflecting all default and user-provided fields, ready for client usage.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo item in the todo_list_todos table. It requires the unique identifier of the todo (id, a UUID) and accepts update data for fields such as title, description, and completion status. The update is strictly limited to the owner; users may only modify their own todos. All updates are applied atomically, maintaining data consistency and privacy boundaries defined in business logic. Fails if the todo does not exist or the user lacks ownership rights.
operations.description:
Update the details of a specific todo item by its unique identifier. The operation allows the owner to change the title, optionally update the description, and toggle the is_completed status. All modifications are timestamped by updating the updated_at field.

Security is critical: only the authenticated owner of the todo may perform this operation. The update is immediate and applies all provided fields atomically. Users cannot update todos they do not own; authorization failure will be returned otherwise.

This API integrates directly with the todo_list_todos table, using the id for targeting. Any change to the todo's content or completion status is reflected in the response, ensuring full data transparency for the user. Related operations include GET for retrieval, PATCH for search, and DELETE for removal. Validation errors, non-existent todos, or ownership violations result in clear error responses.
operations.summary: Update the details of a todo item (todo_list_todos)

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item (UUID, global scope)

requestBody.description: The updated data for the todo item, including title, description, and completion status.

responseBody.description: The updated todo item as persisted in the system.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A todo item record must exist before it can be updated. The todo is created by POST /todoList/user/todos and then can be updated by this operation.

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a todo item from the todo_list_todos table. It requires the unique identifier (id, a UUID) of the targeted todo. Only the owner of a todo is permitted to initiate deletion, ensuring strict privacy and ownership boundaries as enforced by business rules. Deletion is immediate and irreversible, as the design intentionally omits any soft-delete or recovery mechanism per privacy-focused MVP requirements.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a todo item by its unique identifier. This operation enforces user ownership strictly: only the owner of a todo can perform deletion. Deleted todos are irrecoverable as the database is explicitly configured for immediate, destructive removal without any soft-delete or trash features.

On successful deletion, the system returns confirmation or the removed entity's details as appropriate for auditing. Unauthorized requests—due to lack of ownership or missing todo—trigger detailed error responses. Authorization is enforced at the controller and service layers.

This API works directly on the todo_list_todos table using the id field. It is part of the CRUD set for managing personal todos, alongside operations for creation, update, and retrieval. Design choices guarantee that user privacy and data boundaries are always respected.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item (UUID, global scope)

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A todo item record must exist before it can be deleted. The todo is created by POST /todoList/user/todos and then can be deleted by this operation.

authorizations.name: user
authorizations.description: A registered user who can create, view, update, and delete their own todos. Can log in and out via API. Has no access to other users’ data. Can reset their password. All actions are limited to their personal scope.

current.description:
Current page number within the paginated result set.

This field is used by clients to identify which page they are currently viewing or have requested. The first page typically starts at 1. If the result set is empty, this value may default to 0.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records returned per page.

This value defines the size of each page of results. Clients can use this to control how many items they receive at once from the backend. Typical default and maximum values may be determined by system settings or business rules.

records.description:
Total number of records matching the query criteria in the data set.

This value allows the client application to understand the overall result set size, enabling the implementation of page navigation and end‐of‐list detection.

pages.description:
Total number of available result pages given the current query and pagination limit.

This value is computed as the ceiling of records divided by limit. For example, if 55 records and limit of 20, pages equals 3.

IPage.IPagination.description:
Represents page metadata for paginated API results.

Provided in API responses where collections are returned. Encapsulates context for pagination, including the currently viewed page, the per-page limit, total result count, and pages available. Clients should use this structure to implement pagination controls and provide user feedback regarding list navigation.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

ITodoListUser.ICreate.description:
Defines the payload for registering a new user (actor) account for the Todo List application.

This type is used in the public registration (join) endpoint to onboard a user. Fields are derived strictly from the todo_list_users Prisma schema, with no extra properties. Email must be unique and comply with all validation rules. The user supplies a plain password, which the backend securely hashes; password must fulfil all requirements as described in requirements and field descriptions. No profile, role, or additional data is supported.

Required fields include a user email and a plain password, following the business requirements for unique identification and credential management. All validation (uniqueness, presence, maximum lengths, sanitation) matches the todo_list_users Prisma model and business rules. Account will immediately be active if all field checks pass.

email.description: User's unique email address for registration and authentication. Must comply with RFC 5322 and system-level email constraints (max 254 chars, non-empty). Used as the login name and for password recovery notifications.

password.description: Plain password for user registration. At least 8 characters. The system hashes this value before storing and never logs or exposes it. Password policy (length, complexity) is strictly enforced per requirements; never stored or transmitted after registration.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Returned as the response from successful user registration, login, or refresh. Contains both authentication tokens and identity fields for the user actor.

The user ID is unique per user and matches todo_list_users.id. The token data structure contains JWT access and refresh tokens as well as session meta information derived from the user session schema. Only the fields present in these schemas are included.

This type enables authenticated API usage for the Todo List application. The tokens are used for subsequent requests; the id is the authoritative reference for the user's authentication identity. No password or sensitive credential fields are ever present in responses. All session and audit metadata included here are extracted from session schema field definitions.

id.description: The unique user identifier, referencing todo_list_users.id.

email.description: User's unique email address. Used for authentication and system notifications. Must be unique across all accounts and cannot change to an existing value. Valid per RFC 5322. Maximum 254 characters.

User's unique email address for registration and authentication. Must be unique and required at account creation. Used for login, notifications, and password reset workflows. Email addresses are validated for format and length per business policy constraints.

password.description: Plaintext password for user authentication. Submitted via API and never stored as-is; backend hashes using a secure algorithm such as bcrypt. Minimum of 8 and maximum of 72 characters as required by security standards. Password must not be logged or returned in any response.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session tracking (OPTIONAL - server can extract, but client may provide for SSR). Can be either IPv4 or IPv6 string form.
Client IP address for session tracking (OPTIONAL - server can extract, but client may provide for SSR). Can be either IPv4 or IPv6 string form.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking (OPTIONAL - server can extract, but client may provide for SSR). Can be either IPv4 or IPv6 string form.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) - MANDATORY. The URI at which login was initiated; used for authenticating session origin and for logging.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) - MANDATORY. Indicates the page from which the user arrived to the login endpoint.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
Login credentials for an existing user from todo_list_users Prisma schema. Used for authentication via /auth/user/login. Requires an email and password that map exactly to user table fields. On successful authentication, issues JWT tokens and creates a user session as defined by requirements. Session context (href, referrer, ip) is mandatory for application audit and security policy compliance.

Email and password are validated per business rules and schema constraints, with session context required for logging/audit. IP is optional and can be supplied by client or extracted by server.

refresh_token.description: Refresh token string as provided on prior authentication. Must be exact value per issued token and validated for presence, type, and security constraints. Used as the only required field for token refresh operations. The token is validated server-side for authenticity, expiration, and session linkage.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
DTO for user token refresh operations. Includes only the refresh token field. The refresh_token property is a string matching the one issued at previous login or join operations. Used to request a new JWT token set from /auth/user/refresh.

No other fields are permitted or required. The DTO is validated for required presence and minimum secure token length.

email.description: Filter by user's unique email address. Supports exact or partial matches for administrative searching. Must conform to RFC 5322 format. Maximum 254 characters. Used in security, compliance, and audit scenarios.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Must be at least 1. Controls which result page is returned when retrieving lists of users.

limit.description: Maximum number of user results per page. User listings are paginated and this restricts the maximum count per page. Should not exceed 100 for performance and privacy.

oneOf.description: Field to sort the results by. Supported values: 'email', 'created_at'. Controls the column used for sorting returned users.
Field to sort the results by. Supported values: 'email', 'created_at'. Controls the column used for sorting returned users.

sort_by.description: Field to sort the results by. Supported values: 'email', 'created_at'. Controls the column used for sorting returned users.

oneOf.description: Sort order: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Applied to the field specified in 'sort_by'.
Sort order: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Applied to the field specified in 'sort_by'.

sort_order.description: Sort order: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Applied to the field specified in 'sort_by'.

ITodoListUser.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination request parameters for retrieving a list of users from the Todo List system.

Allows administrators to filter users by email address, control pagination, and sort the list. This structure supports data minimization and strict privacy standards; no sensitive user or system fields are accepted. Filtering and sorting controls are designed solely for the administrative audit and compliance use case.

id.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each user account. UUID generated at registration.

email.description: User's unique email address. Used for authentication and system notifications. Must be unique across all accounts and cannot change to an existing value. Valid per RFC 5322. Maximum 254 characters.

ITodoListUser.description:
User account entity for the Todo List application.

Represents a registered user in the system. Each user is uniquely identified by a UUID primary key and an email address, which acts as the main identifier for authentication and notification. This schema intentionally omits password hashes or internal authentication data for security; such fields are only ever handled server-side and are never leaked via API responses.

Account information is strictly minimal by business requirement: no names, profile info, or roles are stored, and all account deletion is irreversible. This entity is used for system audit, inspection, and detail presentation in administrative contexts only.

email.description: The unique email address to be set for this user account if updated. This value must be unique across all user records, follows RFC 5322 rules, and is subject to length and format validation enforced both at API and storage levels. If provided, replaces the prior value. Mapped to the `email` column of the `todo_list_users` table. Providing this field is optional; omit when not updating email.

password.description: The new plain password to be set for this user, if changed. Backend will securely hash this value and store only the resulting hash in the `password_hash` field of the table. Never transmit a hash directly via API—only supply the cleartext password here. Providing a value here will invalidate all existing user sessions as per security policy. Optional; omit when not updating password.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description: Patch/update DTO for the todo_list_users table. Allows for partial updates: either or both the `email` and `password` fields may be supplied on update via PATCH or PUT requests. At least one property must be provided; otherwise, the update will be rejected. All inputs are fully validated. Changing a user's password triggers session invalidation. This schema never exposes stored hashes or authentication internals, only accepting explicit update instructions for end-user mutable fields.

page.description: Page number for paginated session listing, starting from 1. Default is 1 if not specified.

limit.description: Max number of session records per page. Maximum allowed is 100; default is 20.

oneOf.description: Session field to sort results by. Common values: created_at, expired_at, ip, href. If not provided, defaults to created_at.

sortBy.description: Session field to sort results by. Common values: created_at, expired_at, ip, href. If not provided, defaults to created_at.

oneOf.description: Sort order for the listing. Either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).
Sort order for the listing. Either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).

order.description: Sort order for the listing. Either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).

filterIp.description: Optional filter to search for sessions originating from a particular IP address.

filterReferrer.description: Optional filter to search for sessions that originated from a particular referrer URL.

filterHref.description: Optional filter to search for sessions that began on a specific connection URL.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description: Request schema for searching, filtering, sorting, and paginating session records associated with a user in the Todo List application.

id.description: Primary key uniquely identifying this session record. Matches the `id` field in `todo_list_user_sessions` table.

user.description: Summary view of the owner user. Provides privacy-preserved user identification (id/email) for multi-user displays or references.

ip.description: The IP address from which the session was established. Used for security and audit tracing.

href.description: The full URL of the client connection at session start. Captured to provide context for the session's origin.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating the previous location before authentication or session establishment. Used for session context and debugging.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created. Used for audit and ordering.

expired_at.description: Optional timestamp marking when the session expired or was terminated. Nullable. Used for session lifecycle enforcement.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
User session tracking record for the Todo List application.

Represents a single authentication session for an individual user. Includes session context metadata: IP, creation and expiration timestamps, connection href, and HTTP referrer. Used for audit, traceability and security workflows. The session record is always linked to an owning user account, referenced as a summary object. This entity contains no credential or private application data.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Must be 1 or greater. Controls which page of todos is returned.

limit.description: Maximum number of todos per page. Controls result set size for pagination. Maximum 100.

is_completed.description: If true, filters to completed todos; if false, filters to uncompleted todos. Optional – omitting means no completion-status filter is applied.

title.description: Optional case-insensitive substring match filter for todo title.

created_from.description: Inclusive lower bound for creation timestamp filter (ISO8601); returns todos created after or at this date/time. Optional.

created_to.description: Inclusive upper bound for creation timestamp filter (ISO8601); returns todos created before or at this date/time. Optional.

updated_from.description: Inclusive lower bound for last update timestamp filter (ISO8601); returns todos updated after or at this date/time. Optional.

updated_to.description: Inclusive upper bound for last update timestamp filter (ISO8601); returns todos updated before or at this date/time. Optional.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Accepts either 'created_at' or 'updated_at'.
Field to sort results by. Accepts either 'created_at' or 'updated_at'.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Accepts either 'created_at' or 'updated_at'.

oneOf.description: Ordering direction for sort field ('asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending).
Ordering direction for sort field ('asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending).

sort_order.description: Ordering direction for sort field ('asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending).

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination/filter information for retrieving a user's todos in the Todo List application.

All filters apply only to todos owned by the authenticated user. Supports querying by completion state, title substring, creation/update date ranges. Pagination and sorting controls are included for efficient listing and user experience. All parameters are optional – supply only those filters desired.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Globally unique identifier for this todo item. Must be a valid UUID assigned automatically by the database on creation. Used to reference the todo across APIs and persistent storage.

title.description: Required title of the todo. Must be 1 to 255 non-whitespace characters. Serves as the main identifying label for the user's task.

oneOf.description: Optional extended notes for the todo, up to 1024 characters. Provides additional context or instructions for the user's private use.
Description can be omitted if not supplied by the user.

description.description: Optional extended notes for the todo, up to 1024 characters. Provides additional context or instructions for the user's private use. If not present, this field will be null.

is_completed.description: True if the todo is marked completed by the user, false otherwise. Used for workflow and list filtering.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the todo was created. Used for ordering and audit purposes, set automatically on insert.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the todo. Updated on modification of title, description, or completion status, set automatically by the system.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Core business entity representing a personal todo item owned by a registered user.

Stores all user-created tasks for the Todo List application. Every todo is linked to exactly one user through the todo_list_users table, guaranteeing strict per-user privacy and ownership boundaries. Fields include a unique identifier, a required textual title, and an optional description for expanded task notes. Only the owner may read, update, or delete their own todos; cross-user access is strictly prohibited by design.

Completion state is indicated by a boolean is_completed flag, enabling users to filter or display completed and active todos. Each todo records its creation and last modification timestamps to facilitate ordered listings and update tracking. Deletion occurs as an immediate, irreversible operation with no soft delete or recovery feature—a requirement explicitly defined for privacy and simplicity in the MVP.

title.description: Required title of the todo. Must be 1 to 255 non-whitespace characters. Serves as the main identifying label for the user's task.

oneOf.description: Optional extended notes for the todo, up to 1024 characters. Provides additional context or instructions for the user's private use.
Description can be omitted if not supplied by the user.

description.description: Optional extended notes for the todo, up to 1024 characters. Provides additional context or instructions for the user's private use. If not present, this field will be null.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Request body structure for creating a new todo item.

Allows the authenticated user to create a new task in their personal todo list. Requires a non-empty title and optionally accepts a description, both of which must comply with the validation rules of the todo_list_todos schema. The new todo is always owned by the requesting user; ownership, system fields, and association to the user are handled automatically by the backend and must never be supplied by the client.

Clients must not supply the owner or completion status—those are managed explicitly by the system based on authentication context and business rules.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Schema for updating an existing todo item in the todo_list_todos table.

Allows the authenticated owner to modify selected fields—title, description, or completion status—of a specific todo. Ownership and privacy are strictly enforced; only the todo's owner may update. Each update is atomically applied, and modification is timestamped in updated_at.

No other fields may be changed, and users cannot update todos they do not own. All validation is enforced according to the business rules and the Prisma database schema.

title.description: New or replacement title for the todo item. Must be 1 to 255 non-whitespace characters. Acts as the main label for the user's personal task.

oneOf.description: Optional extended notes for the todo, up to 1024 characters. Used for additional private context or instructions.
Null indicates no description is set or description should be removed.

description.description: Optional extended notes for the todo, up to 1024 characters. Can be set to null to remove description.

is_completed.description: Indicates if the todo is marked done (true) or active (false). Updated by the owner to signal workflow progress.

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description: Summary view of a user for the Todo List application. Immutable, non-sensitive properties only. Used for session reference, ownership, and display.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user. Primary key from todo_list_users.id. Used for references, audit logs, and entity ownership tracking. Always present and generated by the system.

email.description: User's unique email address used for registration and authentication. Always present, must be a valid email. Used only as a public identifier, not as an authentication credential in this context.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description: Summary view of a user session for the Todo List application. Used to present non-sensitive session metadata in lists or for audit purposes.

id.description: Unique session identifier. Primary key from todo_list_user_sessions.id. Used for session lookup, list display, and device/session management. Always present and generated by the system.

user.description: Summary information of the owning user. Always references the user who owns this session. Used for context in audit logs and session lists. Does not expose user credentials or personal data.

ip.description: IP address where the session was established. Used for audit logging and device/source context. Always present. Format: IPv4 or IPv6 as captured by server (e.g. '192.168.0.10' or '2001:0db8::1').

href.description: Full client URL at the time of session creation. Used for establishing session context and debugging unusual connection flows. Always present, typically an absolute URL including scheme (e.g. 'https://demo.todo.com/app/login') or the page where login started.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating where the user came from. Always present. Useful for understanding session entry points and authentication flows.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of session creation. Used for audit logs, session history, or ordering session lists. Always captured when the session is created.

oneOf.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the session expired (if any). Present if session naturally expired or was explicitly terminated. Nullable if session is ongoing or active.
Value is null if the session has not expired.

expired_at.description: Expiration timestamp for the session if any, else null.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description: Summary view of a todo item for the Todo List application. Suitable for list views and references without full details.

id.description: Unique identifier for this todo. Primary key from todo_list_todos.id. Always present and generated by the system.

user.description: Summary view of the owner user. Provides privacy-preserved user identification (id/email) for multi-user displays or references.

title.description: Main title of the todo item. Always present in summary. Used for fast lookup and display in lists. Validated: 1 to 255 non-whitespace characters.

is_completed.description: Completion status for this todo. True if user has completed; false otherwise. Used for state grouping/filtering in lists.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime when the todo was created. Used for audit, ordering, and recency-based displays.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime of most recent modification. Updated on any title, completion, or property change.
